title: Hunter Henry agrees to a two-year extension with the Patriots
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Hunter Henry signed a two-year extension with the Patriots worth up to $20 million.
The extension includes $14.5 million in guaranteed money and a $4.2 million signing bonus.
Henry has 259 receptions and 26 touchdowns since joining the Patriots in 2021.

title: 83-year-old drives Jaguar into Acton CVS, causing major damage
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: An 83-year-old woman crashed a Jaguar into a CVS in Acton, causing significant damage to the store on Saturday.
The driver and her 88-year-old passenger were unharmed; the store remains closed pending repairs.
Acton Police have requested the woman's driving license be suspended due to immediate threat concerns.

title: Logan runway closure this fall could mean more flight delays
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Logan Airport's Runway 27 will close for 75 days starting August 31 for safety upgrades.
Construction includes installing an EMAS to stop overrunning planes, expected to finish before Thanksgiving.
The runway closure may cause travel delays and increase flight noise over nearby communities.

title: One dead, 3 injured in head-on crash on the Cape
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A head-on crash in Sandwich, Massachusetts, killed one person and injured three others on Sunday night.
The collision involved a 2011 Toyota Prius heading west and a 2017 Toyota RAV4 heading east on Farmersville Road.
The Prius driver died at Cape Cod Hospital; the RAV4 occupants sustained nonlife-threatening injuries.

title: Driver on South Shore narrowly escaped before commuter train totaled his Camry
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A driver delivering packages mistakenly drove onto railroad tracks in Cohasset, causing a train to crash into his vehicle.
The accident occurred around 12:23 a.m. Sunday on the Greenbush Line; the driver exited safely before the collision.
The 2016 Toyota Camry was totaled; no injuries were reported among the train's 15 passengers or crew.

title: Livestream: Lindsay Clancy murder trial continues with psychiatrist under cross-examination
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Lindsay Clancy's murder trial continues with her former psychiatrist, Dr. Jennifer Tufts, under cross-examination.
Tufts testified Clancy denied suicidal or homicidal thoughts before the January 2023 incident in Duxbury.
Clancy is using an insanity defense, citing postpartum mental illness and medication issues as factors.

title: For $415k, you can live in a New England community library
author: Megan Johnson
bullets: The Tyler Free Library in Foster, R.I., built in 1850, is for sale for $415,000.
Previously a schoolhouse, the 1,760 sq. ft. building sits on one acre and has a fireplace and half-bathroom.
The library's books are not included in the sale; they will move to the Foster Public Library.

title: Patriots 53-man roster projection 1.0: Will New England really stick with 7 receivers?
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: New England Patriots could keep seven wide receivers, with Kayshon Boutte's future uncertain amid trade considerations.
Three quarterbacks likely to be kept: Drake Maye, Tommy DeVito, and Behren Morton due to camp performance.
In crowded cornerback group, New England adds depth amid Carlton Davis’s injury doubts with six cornerbacks retained.

title: Adley Rutschman could make his Red Sox debut in coming days
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Adley Rutschman, acquired by the Red Sox from the Orioles on August 3, could debut against the Blue Jays this week.
Rutschman played rehab games with Triple-A Worcester, traveling with Boston as they face Toronto at Rogers Centre.
Manager Chad Tracy stated Rutschman won't play Monday but could join later in the Toronto series after assessment.

title: Healey signs bill allowing state to take Norwood Hospital through eminent domain
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Gov. Maura Healey signed a bill enabling the state to seize Norwood Hospital through eminent domain.
Starting Nov. 1, DCAMM can take the property from Medical Properties Trust and lease it to a nonprofit.
Norwood Hospital has been vacant since 2020 floods, and construction halted after Steward Health Care's bankruptcy.
